mex-r3.label: MEX scaffold and product hooks, semantic extra installed (prompt recipe R3)

tasks.prompt: The step editor lets me save a Liquid expression that later breaks the preview, and the reported issue is hard to understand. Make authoring-time checks agree with rendering so syntax that cannot be rendered is reported as a compilation issue before delivery. Keep valid single-quoted expressions, multiline tags, and JSON-encoded rich content working, with useful issue locations for nested expressions.

Custom SMTP integrations need an editable TLS-options JSON object instead of a plain text value. Let users configure it in the integration form, reject malformed JSON and non-object values before saving, and keep the credential definition and form behavior consistent. Improve the setup guidance so TLS, DKIM, and troubleshooting are understandable.

Two connections to the same chat or webhook service currently share the same custom content. Let a workflow author provide different custom content for each connection while retaining service-wide defaults and trigger-time overrides. Make saving, rendering, sending, previewing, duplicating, and syncing workflows agree. Renaming a connection should retain its custom content; disconnected entries should remain visible. Keep existing content working and prevent internal transport bookkeeping from appearing in provider payloads.

Liquid whitespace control is not behaving correctly in JSON-based step controls: dash tags leave surrounding newlines behind. Fix rendering so whitespace-trimming tags behave as they do in ordinary Liquid, while plain tags keep their whitespace and newlines or literal backslash sequences supplied in values round-trip correctly. Keep callback behavior and error reporting compatible.

Push steps need the custom-content editing and preview support already available for chat. Add a schema-backed editor for Expo and an escape hatch for the other push services, preserve ordinary title/body output, and carry the custom payload through sending. Device destinations must still come from subscriber tokens, and documented Expo options must survive key conversion correctly.

Older notification feeds and message responses still expose unsafe click destinations from already-stored notifications, even though the current inbox protects them. Cover the legacy read and action-update responses as well. Remove unsafe destinations and invalid window targets from both the notification and its buttons, keep labels and other action data, preserve valid destinations, and avoid changing the stored notification just to return a safe response.

Add Google Chat as a supported chat delivery service, including its integration configuration, subscriber webhook destinations, delivery construction, and documentation. It should work with both new endpoint records and the legacy stored webhook credential, and custom-content previews should fall back to the normal message text consistently.

Our email webhook verifier uses a binary HMAC key, but signatures currently assume that the stored key is plain text. Let an integration select plain text, base64, or hex key encoding, retaining the existing default. Carry the setting from saved credentials through delivery, sign with the decoded bytes, and reject encodings that decode to an empty key. Equivalent binary keys should produce equivalent signatures.

Commands copied from a specific agent's setup page should reconnect that agent instead of asking me to choose an agent and runtime again. They also need to work on local dashboards: browser login should return to that dashboard, staging should use the release-candidate command, and regional production APIs should stay regional. Keep the copied chat command and self-hosted scaffold command consistent, and fail clearly if the requested agent is missing.

The dashboard's chat onboarding currently makes me run setup twice and choose information I already supplied. Produce one connection command that retains the chosen runtime, channel, and existing agent. The command-line flow should reuse that agent without a picker, and copied instructions should not ask for the same choices again. Keep the separate scaffold step for other channels where it is still needed.

Scaffolded browser and self-hosted agent projects can end up with incompatible SDK releases on staging or local development. Make their generated dependencies use the appropriate prerelease distribution consistently, while production scaffolds keep stable dependencies and the command itself keeps its own release channel. Carry the selected environment through each scaffold path and avoid mixing local workspace aliases with downloaded SDK versions.

The chat onboarding prompt and command-line handoff instructions disagree about what happens after connecting. Route copied setup instructions through the dedicated chat flow and keep success messages and handoffs consistent for managed, self-hosted, embedded, already-connected, and skipped outcomes. Only ask for an embed handoff when that outcome actually produced one, and preserve the existing channel choices for other flows.

Newly scaffolded conversational projects using the AI SDK wait for a complete answer instead of streaming it. Update the generated handler and browser example so responses stream progressively using the supported response interface, and make the setup instructions and code-generation guidance agree. Preserve conversation context and metadata when generating the response.
